title: A Systematic Approach for Multi-objective Double-side Clock Tree Synthesis
problem: As semiconductor devices scale, utilizing back-side silicon space via double-side clock trees requires systematic design resource allocation and multi-objective optimization, but existing tools only hack single-side approaches.
motivation: Back-side utilization is emerging as a key trend to overcome conventional area and power constraints in future advanced-node ICs, enabling better clock distribution across both metal layers.
method: The approach performs hierarchical clock routing with concurrent buffers and nano Through-Silicon-Via (nTSV) insertion, followed by skew refinement on double-side metal layers. It systematically allocates resources across back- and front-side, jointly optimizing latency, skew, wirelength, and via/buffer count through a unified optimization framework.
key_novelty: First systematic multi-objective approach to double-side clock tree synthesis using nTSVs, jointly optimizing latency, skew, wirelength, and resource utilization rather than adapting single-side heuristics.
contributions: Hierarchical clock routing algorithm for double-side metal layers with systematic resource allocation.
Concurrent buffers and nTSV insertion with multi-objective optimization.
Skew refinement stage optimizing latency, wirelength, and buffer/via count simultaneously.

metrics.other: improved latency, skew, wirelength, reduced buffers and nTSVs vs SOTA

primary_theme: double-side clock tree synthesis with nTSVs
